vowel_formants.speaker: adult male (mean of 10 Seoul speakers aged 18 to 27), vowels in the frame hVda
vowel_formants.notes: F1 and F2 of /o/ and /u/ were checked against the quotation of Yang (1996) in Han & Kang (2013); the other values are given from the compiler's record of the same table and should be checked against the original before critical use. The separate /e/ and /ɛ/ of this older sample have merged for most speakers today, and /o/ has moved closer to /u/ in younger speakers.

contrasts: three-way contrast in stops and affricates, all voiceless at the start of a word: lenis /p t k t͡ɕ/, fortis /p͈ t͈ k͈ t͈͡ɕ/, aspirated /pʰ tʰ kʰ t͡ɕʰ/
two-way contrast in fricatives: lenis /s/ against fortis /s͈/
back unrounded /ɯ ʌ/ against back rounded /u o/
no lexical stress, tone or (for most speakers born after about 1970) vowel length
allophony: lenis stops and the lenis affricate are voiced [b d ɡ d͡ʑ] between voiced sounds inside an accentual phrase and voiceless, weakly to moderately aspirated at its start

at the start of an accentual phrase a vowel after a fortis or aspirated consonant, /s/ or /h/ is higher in pitch than after a lenis consonant or sonorant, by about 3 semitones on average and more for younger speakers (Kang 2014); this pitch difference is now the main cue separating lenis from aspirated stops
in a syllable coda only [p̚ t̚ k̚ m n ŋ l] occur: all coronal obstruents and /h/ become unreleased [t̚], labials [p̚], velars [k̚]
a coda obstruent becomes a nasal before a nasal (국물 [kuŋmul], 입니다 [imnida], 먹는 [mʌŋnɯn])
/n/ next to /l/ becomes [l] (신라 [ɕilla]); /l/ after a consonant other than /n l/ becomes [n] (심리 [ɕimni], 독립 [toŋnip])
a lenis obstruent after an obstruent becomes fortis (학교 [hak̚k͈jo])
/h/ next to a lenis stop merges with it into an aspirated stop (좋다 [t͡ɕotʰa]); /h/ between voiced sounds is weak [ɦ] or dropped (좋아요)
/t tʰ/ before a suffix beginning with /i/ become [d͡ʑ t͡ɕʰ] (같이 [kat͡ɕʰi])
/s s͈/ are alveolo-palatal [ɕ ɕ͈] before /i/ and /j/
/l/ is a tap [ɾ] between vowels and at the start of a syllable, and a lateral [l], often retroflex, in a coda and when doubled
word-initial nasals are weakly nasal, close to voiced stops
/ɰi/ is [i] after a consonant and often [e] as the genitive particle
/e/ and /ɛ/ have merged for most speakers; older /ø y/ are now [we wi]
phonotactics: only one consonant in the onset and one in the coda; written double codas are simplified unless a vowel follows
in native and Sino-Korean words /l/ does not begin a word, and /n/ is dropped before initial /i j/ (South Korean standard)
a coda consonant is carried over to the onset of the next syllable when that syllable starts with a vowel

stress.rule: Seoul Korean has no lexical stress; the unit of prominence is the accentual phrase, marked by its tone pattern. Older accounts that put stress on a heavy first syllable, and otherwise on the second, describe the rising start of that phrase.
stress.cues: pitch pattern of the accentual phrase and lengthening at the end of intonational phrases; no stress-linked vowel reduction

rhythm.notes: Lengthening is strong on the last syllable of an intonational phrase and weak at the end of an accentual phrase.

length.notes: A vowel length contrast in the first syllable of a word (눈 'eye' short, 눈 'snow' long) belongs to the older standard and is lost for most speakers. Fortis consonants have a much longer closure than lenis ones between vowels, and doubled sonorants across a syllable boundary (ll, nn, mm) are long.

voice_onset_time_ms.source: Lisker & Abramson 1964 (word-initial stops, speaker of the older generation)
voice_onset_time_ms.notes: The lenis and aspirated values were checked against a later quotation; the fortis values are from the compiler's record of the same table. These values describe the older system. In present-day Seoul speech aspirated and lenis stops have nearly merged in VOT: the estimated mean for aspirated stops falls from 93 ms (men born 1932) to 53 ms (men born 1984) and from 69 to 46 ms for women, and the aspirated-lenis difference shrinks from 31 ms to under 6 ms over the same birth years (Kang 2014). A synthesiser aiming at present-day speech should use about 50 to 65 ms for both series, under 20 ms for fortis stops, and rely on pitch to separate lenis from aspirated.

intonation.declarative: each accentual phrase has the pattern T H ... L H, where the first tone T is high after a fortis or aspirated consonant, /s/ or /h/ and low otherwise; the final H of the last phrase is replaced by a low or falling boundary tone (L% or HL%)
intonation.yes_no_question: high or rising boundary tone on the last syllable (H% or LH%)
intonation.wh_question: most often a rising boundary tone (LH% or H%), sometimes a falling one (HL%); the question word usually begins an accentual phrase that takes in the following words
intonation.continuation: the high tone that ends each accentual phrase, and a high boundary tone (H% or LH%) at the end of a non-final intonational phrase, with lengthening of the last syllable
intonation.accent_shape: no pitch accents; tones mark the edges of the accentual phrase: low or high on the first syllable, high on the second, low on the penultimate and high on the last
intonation.notes: Phrases of fewer than four syllables realise only part of the pattern (for example LH, LHH or HH). The boundary tone inventory of the K-ToBI model includes L%, H%, LH%, HL%, LHL%, HLH% and longer sequences (Jun 1998, 2005).

tone.tone_bearing_unit: first syllable of the accentual phrase

inventory.name: low start (after lenis obstruents, sonorants and vowels)
inventory.description: low on the first syllable, rising to high on the second
inventory.phonation: slightly breathy at vowel onset after lenis stops

inventory.name: high start (after fortis and aspirated obstruents, /s/, /h/)
inventory.description: high on the first and second syllables
inventory.phonation: pressed or tense at vowel onset after fortis consonants; breathy after aspirated ones

sandhi: the pitch of the first syllable is fixed by the laryngeal type of the phrase-initial consonant and is not lexical
in accentual phrases of fewer than four syllables the middle tones are left out or merged
at the end of an intonational phrase the last tone of the accentual phrase gives way to the boundary tone
tone.notes: The pitch after aspirated stops is on average 3.4 semitones above that after lenis stops (2.9 for men, 3.8 for women; 2.2 for speakers born in 1932 and 4.3 for those born in 1984), and after fortis stops 3.2 semitones above (Kang 2014). The Chao numerals are schematic and cover the first two syllables. eSpeak NG defines no tone phonemes for Korean.

phonation: fortis obstruents: long closure, very short VOT and stiff or pressed voice at the start of the next vowel
lenis obstruents: slightly breathy vowel onset and low pitch at the start of a phrase; voiced between voiced sounds
aspirated obstruents: long aspiration and high pitch on the next vowel

problems: lenis ㄱ is reversed: voiced [ɡ] at the start of a word and a voiceless uvular stop [q] between vowels and in codas (고기 is given as [ɡoqi], 한국어 as [hanquqʌ]); ㄷ is voiced [d] everywhere, also word-initially; only ㅂ and ㅈ are voiceless initially and voiced medially
no nasalisation of ㄱ and ㅂ codas before a nasal: 입니다, 감사합니다, 국물 and 먹는 keep a stop
no lateralisation and no change of ㄹ to [n]: 신라, 심리 and 독립 keep a tap after the consonant
ㅅ and ㅆ are the same sound (the fortis phoneme is a copy of the plain one, marked temporary), and neither becomes [ɕ] before i
fortis stops are plain unaspirated stops without long closure or tense voice; word-initial ㄲ uses the uvular stop sample
the consonant has no effect on the pitch of the next vowel, so the main present-day cue to lenis against aspirated stops is missing
prosody is stress-based (first syllable if heavy, otherwise the second) with generic tunes; the accentual phrase pattern and the boundary tones are not modelled
ㅎ plus a lenis stop gives a sequence of two stops (좋다 as [t͡ɕot tʰa]) instead of one aspirated stop, and ㅎ at the start of a syllable is a full [h] also between voiced sounds
coda ㄹ is a velarised lateral
IPA output contains strings that are not IPA, such as p-, t-, tɕ- for fortis and kh, ph for aspirated consonants
the source marks the language as a test (comment 'Korean, TEST' in tr_languages.c) and several phonemes as temporary or TODO
good: Hangul syllables are split into letters, and codas are carried over to a following vowel
coda neutralisation and simplification of double codas (밖, 옷, 없다, 읽다, 닭, 값)
fortis after an obstruent (학교) and palatalisation of ㄷ and ㅌ before i (같이)
separate vowels for ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ ㅔ ㅐ and glide combinations

notes: The accentual phrase, not the word, is the unit that a synthesiser has to model: it sets voicing of lenis stops (voiced inside the phrase), the pitch pattern and the consonant-dependent pitch of the first syllable.
